title: Model Editing at Scale leads to Gradual and Catastrophic Forgetting
forget_metric: edit efficacy / recall of prior edits
low_dose_frontier_quality: good below knee: efficacy ~100% until inflection
near_collapse_behaviour: two-phase: gradual decline then abrupt cliff; ROME knee at 100-800 edits (as low as 10); MEMIT gradual to ~4000 edits; paraphrase detection dies long before the cliff
notes: ~30% of previously edited facts forgotten by 600 ROME edits (sample 1); MEMIT ~10% at same count. Canonical two-phase (gradual->catastrophic) curve; feeds the knee-location prior for H4.

title: Model Editing Harms General Abilities of Large Language Models: Regularization to the Rescue
low_dose_frontier_quality: poor for KN: single edit can zero out tasks; ROME/MEMIT tolerable at small N
near_collapse_behaviour: perturbation compounds: ROME weight elements with delta>0.077 grow 20%(1 edit)->49.2%(5)->72.8%(15); KN collapses after 1 edit on LLaMA-1
notes: RECT regularization retains >94% edit success while protecting downstream — evidence that a repair/regularity term buys real budget. Weight-drift metric is a usable leakage proxy.

title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
low_dose_frontier_quality: acceptable for 1 request for some methods; most degrade by request 2-4
near_collapse_behaviour: GA and NPO collapse to ~zero utility after first requests; utility decreases monotonically with request count for nearly all 8 methods
notes: Sustainability axis = the protocol to copy for H4: 4 sequential folds of 0.8M tokens News corpus; measures utility trend vs request index. Also finds unlearned knowledge resurfaces under paraphrase probing.

title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning (O3: Orthogonal LoRA + OOD detector)
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: O3 at request 3 keeps 78.5/80.9 vs base 88.0/88.7 (ScienceQA) with no retain data
near_collapse_behaviour: GradDif and SOGD emit empty/nonsensical repeated tokens by request 2-3; EUL degrades by request 3
notes: Structural isolation (orthogonal LoRA per request) prevents inter-request interference — supports ordering/isolation levers for keeping each day under budget. Uses no retain data at all.

title: Avoiding Copyright Infringement via Large Language Model Unlearning (Stable Sequential Unlearning)
method_family: task-vector negation + random-labeling loss + weight saliency
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: SSU MMLU 0.6625(step1)->0.6425(step5) i.e. ~0.5%/step absolute, stable to step 10
near_collapse_behaviour: GA collapses by step 5 (MMLU 0.58->0.31 Llama; step 1 on Mistral); Task Vector hits MMLU=0 by step 10 (Llama) / step 5 (Mistral); GradDiff MT-Bench 8.03->4.94 at step 5
notes: Closest analogue to our design: ~1 concept(book)/step for 10 steps on an 8B chat model. SSU's ~0.3-0.5% MMLU loss/step is a direct per-cycle leakage estimate; naive methods knee at 5-10 steps.

title: FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models
method_family: redundancy filtering + adaptive algorithm selection + targeted layers
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: at 300 requests MMLU 65.56 vs retain-model 65.97, GSM8K 57.02 vs 58.83
near_collapse_behaviour: retain utility sags 0.88(60 req)->0.71(120) then plateaus ~0.70-0.72 to 300; GA/RLabel collapse to near zero
notes: Largest sequential-request count found (300). Shows a sag-then-plateau rather than a cliff when interventions are localized/filtered — favourable shape for H4 at our N=30.

title: Adaptive Localization of Knowledge Negation for Continual LLM Unlearning
low_dose_frontier_quality: >95% utility retained after sufficient sequential unlearning
near_collapse_behaviour: some baselines completely lose utility over the same task sequence
notes: ICML 2025. Key idea for us: adapt unlearning intensity to inter-task (concept) relationships — entangled concepts get gentler doses; supports concept-ordering lever. PDF numbers not fully extracted (compressed PDF).

title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
low_dose_frontier_quality: excellent to 3000 edits: original general capability maintained across all metrics
near_collapse_behaviour: MEMIT GLUE F1 approaches zero by 2000 edits; MEMIT efficacy 65.65% vs AlphaEdit 98.90% (LLaMA-3 at 2000)
notes: Projection onto null space of preserved-knowledge keys = mathematically constrained low-leakage intervention; the mechanism our forgetting arm should imitate to stay under budget.

title: Reproducibility Study of AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing
base_model: LLaMA-3-8B, GPT-J, GPT2-XL, Llama3.2-1B/3B, Qwen2.5-3B, Phi3-3.8B, Gemma2-2B
near_collapse_behaviour: knee at ~5000 edits: LLaMA-3-8B BoolQ >0.8 -> <0.1 after 5000; MMLU ~0.6 -> ~0.1 by 10000; protection is bounded not unconditional
notes: Independent confirmation that even the best constrained editor has a finite knee; also tests 1-4B models (closest to gemma-3-4b) where AlphaEdit's advantage does not generalize uniformly.

title: Lifelong Knowledge Editing requires Better Regularization (ENCORE)
utility_metric: MMLU, SST2, MRPC, RTE, CoLA, NLI (every 1000 edits)
low_dose_frontier_quality: ENCORE holds downstream through 10000 edits; edit score 92.57 at 10k (Llama-2-7B)
near_collapse_behaviour: MEMIT norm grows 10x by 10k edits, edited-layer share of residual stream rises from ~1% to 7-40%, edit score ~81->~50 (Llama-3-8B); baselines degrade at 3000-5000 edits
notes: Identifies the accumulation mechanism itself: monotone norm growth = a measurable, non-un-leakable damage odometer. Norm/activation-share tracking is a cheap daily leakage meter for our runs.

title: Perturbation-Restrained Sequential Model Editing (PRUNE)
low_dose_frontier_quality: restraining condition number preserves general ability during sequential editing
near_collapse_behaviour: unrestrained condition numbers grow with edit count and progressively disrupt original associations
notes: Second independent accumulation mechanism (condition-number growth). Supports H4 lever: bounding per-day perturbation keeps cumulative damage sublinear.

title: A Comprehensive Study of Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models (KnowEdit)
low_dose_frontier_quality: current methods manage single/batch edits with minimal cognitive disruption
near_collapse_behaviour: fluency/locality degrade before edit success does in erasure settings
notes: Benchmark/taxonomy source (KnowEdit datasets incl. erasure). Useful for metric definitions (locality = our collateral); weak on long sequential sweeps.

title: CURaTE: Continual Unlearning in Real Time with Ensured Preservation of LLM Knowledge
low_dose_frontier_quality: near-perfect: TOFU stage 3 retain 0.961 vs base 0.973 across 10 RETURN stages
near_collapse_behaviour: GA retain 0.973->0.003 and GradDiff ->0.000 by TOFU stage 3; CURaTE flat because weights never move
notes: Guardrail-style baseline: zero accumulation because nothing is edited — an upper-bound control arm, but does not satisfy our weight-level erasure requirement (recoverable by removing the gate).
